title: Bound the ChannelManager last-activity map with an LRU cap

claims.statement: Claude Code (claude-code) is the source-producing agent for CHG-0072 under human principal @rodrigoteamx, on the 2026-08-24 directive 'dale al merge y a lo que sigue' — the sixth hardening fix, closing the ChannelManager unbounded-map finding. This does not authorize automatic merge of CHG-0072.
claims.evidence: AGENTS.md, profile.json actors and the 2026-08-24 user directive.

claims.statement: The hardening audit found ChannelManager.lastActivity grows without eviction: it is set on subscribe and broadcast and never deleted, even after the channel itself is removed when its subscribers reach zero, so a long-lived process that has seen many distinct channels leaks memory.
claims.evidence: server/src/services/ChannelManager.ts prior subscribe/broadcast/unsubscribe; the 2026-08-24 hardening-audit finding hardening-channelmanager-eviction.

claims.statement: The lastActivity map is intentionally retained after a channel empties (it feeds the Show live/lastActive projection so 'last live 5m ago' still reads true), so the fix is an LRU size cap (default 10000 entries) rather than delete-on-empty: a touchLastActivity helper re-inserts the key at the most-recent position and evicts the oldest once over the cap, and is called from subscribe and broadcast.
claims.evidence: server/src/services/ChannelManager.ts touchLastActivity and the lastActivity comment.

claims.statement: Governed discovery rejected the naive delete-on-empty fix because the code comment shows lastActivity must survive an empty channel for the live projection; an LRU cap bounds memory while preserving recent activity — an evicted, least-recently-active channel is by definition no longer live.
claims.evidence: server/src/services/ChannelManager.ts lastActivity comment (survives a channel going empty) versus the delete-on-empty alternative.

claims.statement: A small-cap instance that evicts the oldest by recency (LRU, proven by re-touching a key so it survives), stays bounded across 100 channels at a cap of 5, and still reports activity for a channel that went empty, proves the bound preserves the survives-empty semantic.

The default cap is 10000 entries, far above realistic concurrent-plus-recent channel counts; getLastActivity has no current consumer (it is a future live-projection API), but the survives-empty semantic is honored for when it does.
claims.evidence: server/src/services/ChannelManager.ts maxLastActivityEntries default; no caller of getLastActivity exists in server/src or studio/src.

claims.statement: The change is server-only and additive: a bounded touch helper, a constructor option, and a test. No protocol or Studio change and no existing behavior regresses.
claims.evidence: git diff of the CHG-0072 branch: server/src/services/ChannelManager.ts and server/tests/unit/channelManagerEviction.test.ts.

successCriteria.statement: The last-activity map is bounded to the cap, evicting the least-recently-active channel.
successCriteria.verification: A test with a cap of 3 subscribes four channels (re-touching one) and asserts the least-recently-active is evicted while the re-touched and recent ones remain; a cap-of-5 test over 100 channels retains exactly five.

successCriteria.statement: Activity survives a channel going empty.
successCriteria.verification: A test subscribes then unsubscribes a channel and asserts getLastActivity still returns a number.
The full server suite passes and the server type-check passes.

definitionOfDone.statement: CHG-0072 records the unbounded-map finding, the survives-empty constraint, and the LRU-cap fix before implementation.
definitionOfDone.evidence: Schema-valid record and deterministic governance compilation.

definitionOfDone.statement: subscribe and broadcast record activity through an LRU-capped helper bounded by a configurable maximum.
A test proves the LRU eviction, the bound across many channels, and the survives-empty semantic; the full server suite passes.
Governance, licensing, lint, type-check, focused and full tests, build, dependency audit and diff checks pass before handoff.
definitionOfDone.evidence: npm run governance:check, npm run check, npm run build, npm audit (0 vulnerabilities), ESLint, type-check and git diff --check; the accept commit is verified by its own pull-request Constitution run before merge.
